etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English piler, from Old French pilier, from Medieval Latin or Vulgar Latin *pilāre (“a pillar”), from Latin pila (“a pillar, pier, mole”).

definitions.definition: (architecture) A large post, often used as supporting architecture.
(figuratively) An essential part of something that provides support.

quote.citation: 1992, Richard Nixon, “The Pacific Triangle”, in Seize the Moment‎[1], Simon & Schuster, →ISBN, →LCCN, →OCLC, page 181:
quote.text: In the Shanghai Communiqué of 1972, we recognized the fact that both Beijing and Taipei viewed Taiwan as part of China but unequivocally expressed our support for a peaceful settlement of the unification issue. While we should not alter the fundamental pillars of our policy, we should consider certain steps that will raise Taiwan's international standing.

quote.citation: 2016, Kenneth Lonergan, Manchester by the Sea, spoken by CJ (Christian Mallen):
quote.text: Star Trek is one of the pillars of modern entertainment.

definitions.definition: (Roman Catholicism) A portable ornamental column, formerly carried before a cardinal, as emblematic of his support to the church.

quote.text: two laye-men seculareache of theym holdynge a pillar In their hondes, steade of a mace

definitions.definition: The centre of the volta, ring, or manege ground, around which a horse turns.
(bodybuilding) The body from the hips over the core to the shoulders.
(geology) A vertical, often spire-shaped, natural rock formation.
To provide with pillars or added strength as if from pillars.

quote.text: Insufficient penetration, or faulty distribution of the blast, may give rise to "pillaring" — that is, the formation of a pillar or column of cold material extending up through the middle of the hearth

quote.citation: 1996, National Academy of Engineering, First annual Symposium on Frontiers of Engineering, page 25:
quote.text: We discovered this new class of compounds in our search for a means of generating porosity by pillaring layered double hydroxides

quote.citation: 1998, Zhong Lin Wang with Zhen Chuan Kang, Functional and smart materials, page 226:
quote.text: In the pillaring-grafting reaction the dimensionality increases by pillaring the organic or precursory polynuclear metal hydroxyl cations into an inorganic layer structured matrix.

quote.citation: 2004, Scott M. Auerbach with Kathleen A. Carrado and Prabir K. Dutta, Handbook of layered materials, page 261:
quote.text: It was then that scientists started to create porosity in the interlayer space of layered clays. developing the first pillared clays with pores in the larger microporous region.
